claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on existing data can accurately predict free energies and thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Machine-learning prediction would significantly reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy systems at temperatures relevant to fusion properties.
A neural-network model will be developed using existing elemental and binary-system data.
The neural network will predict free energies and thermodynamic properties.
The training procedure will preserve faithful free energies for both solid and fluid states.
The training procedure will retain the relevant entropy contributions.
The neural network will learn relationships linking composition and temperature to free energies and other thermodynamic properties.
Learning these relationships will permit rapid property prediction without costly molecular-dynamics simulations.
The model's predictions will be comparable in accuracy to explicit ab initio predictions.
The model will have significantly lower computational cost than explicit ab initio methods.
Explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD are the baseline methods for comparison in multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The proposed method is limited to multicomponent high-entropy systems under high-temperature conditions relevant to fusion.
Prediction accuracy will depend on the quality and quantity of the training data.
Generalization to compositions and conditions not represented in training is uncertain.
The model will be falsified if any key predicted thermodynamic property differs from explicit ab initio results by more than 10%.
